summary: DAY cumulative falsification covered all 12 active-batch companies independently. No thesis is presently falsified outright. The strongest live challenge set is concentration/common-factor exposure, capital intensity/dilution, export/geopolitical policy, pre-revenue commercialization risk, and leverage/business-mix execution. These are explicit present risks or future falsifiers, not generic reasons for perpetual non-readiness. All 12 are advisory ready_for_chief from the red-team lane; underwriting/source gates remain independent.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Launch/manufacturing expansion, M&A and Neutron can compound cash burn and dilution; current evidence identifies the risk without establishing thesis failure.
unknowns: Neutron cash requirement and backlog cancellation economics

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Hyperscaler concentration, export controls and customer custom silicon are the clearest downside paths; disclosed concentration makes the risk measurable rather than hidden.
unknowns: Future restriction breadth and custom-silicon wallet share

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Accelerator software/deployment economics and share persistence remain the principal falsifiers; absence of granular end-customer economics is an underwriting gap, not a red-team contradiction.
unknowns: Normalized accelerator margins and deployment concentration

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Taiwan concentration is a non-diversifiable tail risk and overseas capacity may dilute returns; neither is currently a factual contradiction to the foundry thesis.
unknowns: Overseas fab cost curve and geopolitical event timing

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Export restrictions, customer capex cyclicality and High-NA ROI can impair growth; current evidence supports explicit scenario treatment rather than thesis rejection.
unknowns: Future China/export mix and High-NA customer ROI

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: SoftBank control, related parties, customer concentration and RISC-V substitution are material; current disclosures make these risks visible enough for conservative treatment.
unknowns: RISC-V trajectory and future royalty durability

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Memory-cycle mean reversion and HBM capacity competition are the core failure analogue; high capex amplifies the downside if scarcity normalizes faster than expected.
unknowns: Post-peak margins and competitor capacity response

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Cloud-titan concentration and white-box/custom-fabric substitution remain the key downside paths; concentration is known rather than concealed.
unknowns: Current customer percentages if undisclosed and future substitution rate

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: A very large Meta capacity commitment validates demand but simultaneously creates concentration, financing and execution dependence on timely cluster delivery; contract size must not be mistaken for assured economics.
unknowns: Buildout margin, financing need and termination/volume economics

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Customer/receivables concentration and government-budget dependence can create lumpy growth; current concentration evidence is a risk input, not a contradiction to product relevance.
unknowns: Backlog conversion and government/commercial mix durability

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: The dominant red-team case is dilution-funded runway plus pre-commercial licensing/construction risk: large liquidity does not validate unit economics or commercial timing.
unknowns: Commercial offtake quality, licensing timing and realized plant economics

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Leverage/capital intensity and the transition between self-mining and AI infrastructure can obscure sustainable economics; adjusted EBITDA must not supersede GAAP losses or financing dependence.
unknowns: Fully diluted overhang, AI pipeline conversion and segment capital returns

materialFindings.finding: All 12 companies are advisory ready_for_chief from the adversarial lane because their principal downside paths are identified and no current contradiction independently prevents conservative methodology treatment.
The batch remains highly exposed to a shared AI-capex/hyperscaler regime across NVDA, AMD, TSM, ASML, ARM, MU, ANET and NBIS; ticker count materially overstates factor diversification.

OKLO and RKLB illustrate the same anti-pattern in different sectors: available liquidity or backlog can coexist with substantial future capital needs and milestone risk; those quantities must not be treated as proof of realized economics.

contradictions: Strong demand validation can increase customer concentration and execution dependence rather than reduce risk.
Large liquidity can reflect recent dilution and should not be conflated with self-funded economics.
unknowns: Comparable single-factor stress losses are not canonically modeled across the batch.
Exact customer identities/economics remain undisclosed for several companies.

peerRequests.request: Keep exact reproducibility blockers narrow; do not reopen already identified future falsifiers as generic evidence gaps.
Treat ready_for_chief=true here as adversarial clearance only; preserve underwriting/source gates independently.

accuracyDebates.reason: Batch-level AI-capex correlation should remain visible so apparent diversification does not inflate confidence.
